Urinary Incontinence

stress, urge, overflow, fistula · the postvoid residual splits the differential · cough stress test · drug pairingsWhat is the postvoid residual, and which diagnosis does that number make impossible?

Source vignette Pt – woman with urinary leakage; no pelvic surgery, obstetric injury, malignancy or radiation · Labs – postvoid residual 800 mL · Q – the most likely diagnosis; options spanned overflow, stress and urge incontinence and vesicovaginal fistula

1Presentation
Bottom line
  • The postvoid residual (PVR) splits the differential before any symptom is weighed: under 50 mL is normal, a high residual means overflow
  • A bladder holding 800 mL cannot be draining through a fistula
  • Oxybutynin treats urge incontinence and worsens overflow
What it is

Involuntary loss of urine; stress, urge, overflow, functional, fistula, or a mix

Sort by

The residual (low or high) what sets off the leak: cough, urgency, constant dribbling, or the trip to the toilet

Hands off

Overflow from the prostate: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia and Urinary Retention

2Urgent risks
InfectionUrgency and frequency with dysuria, pyuria and nitrites

If the urinalysis is positive, choose treat the infection; it is not chronic incontinence.

RetentionA high residual with dribbling and recurrent infection

If the bladder does not empty, choose catheterize and stop anticholinergics.

3Differential
Incontinence types, most tempting first
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
Stress incontinenceLeaks with cough, sneeze or lifting; pregnancy, childbirth, menopause, obesityLow residual; leak starts and stops with the cough
Urge incontinence (overactive bladder)Sudden urge, then leakage; frequency, nocturiaLow residual; detrusor overactivity
Overflow incontinenceHesitancy, weak stream, dribbling, recurrent infectionHigh residual: an underactive detrusor or an obstructed outlet
Functional incontinenceDementia or immobility; cannot reach the toiletNormal residual and a normal tract
Vesicovaginal fistulaContinuous leakage; urine pooling in the vaginaAfter surgery, delivery or radiation; dye in the vagina
Normal pressure hydrocephalusIncontinence with a magnetic, wide-based gait and dementiaThe triad: wet, wobbly and wacky; head imaging; sometimes reversible
Mixed incontinenceStress and urge features togetherBoth histories, low residual
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext move
Leaks with cough, low residualStress incontinencePelvic floor exercises, then a pessary, then a midurethral sling
Urgency, low residualUrge incontinenceBladder training, then an antimuscarinic or mirabegron, then botulinum toxin
High residual, enlarged prostateOverflow from outlet obstructionAlpha-blocker
High residual, no obstructionDetrusor underactivityIntermittent catheterization; bethanechol In practiceIn practice: a clinical reference calls bethanechol usually ineffective; catheterization carries the treatment.
Spinal cord lesionAbove the sacral cord: spastic bladder; at the sacral cord: atonic bladderSpastic leaks with urgency; atonic overflows
Rising residual on oxybutyninAnticholinergic retentionStop the drug; check for fecal impaction

Pause point. The bait: stress incontinence from a positive cough test, or a fistula, in a woman with a residual of 800 mL. The residual names overflow; no fistula, surgery, delivery injury or radiation is present.

Practice
  1. 58 yo F, leaks only when coughing, PVR 30, four vaginal deliveries → Stress incontinence → pelvic floor exercises first
  2. 68 yo F, sudden urge then leakage with nocturia, PVR 40 → Urge incontinence from detrusor overactivity
  3. 72 yo M, hesitancy and weak stream, PVR 350, enlarged prostate → Overflow incontinence from outlet obstruction → α-blocker ± 5-α-reductase inhibitor
  4. 28 yo F, continuous leakage two weeks after a difficult delivery, vaginal urine pooling → Vesicovaginal fistula
  5. 84 yo F with dementia, wets before reaching the bathroom, tract normal → Functional incontinence
  6. 68 yo F on oxybutynin with rising PVR and retention → Anticholinergic-induced retention → stop the drug
  7. 45 yo F, urgency and frequency with dysuria, pyuria and nitrites → Urinary tract infection → not chronic incontinence
  8. 40 yo F with multiple sclerosis, mixed retention and urgency → Neurogenic bladder → urodynamics
  9. 32 yo F, T1DM, PVR 800 → Screen for autonomic neuropathy → gastroparesis, orthostatic hypotension and resting tachycardia
Boundary conditions A high PVR (postvoid residual) suggests that overflow is present, not that it is the only mechanism; mixed incontinence is common. A positive cough test may reflect a real coexisting stress component. A PVR is only interpretable when measured after a normal void. PVR thresholds in adults: under 50 mL is normal and argues against overflow; over 100 mL may suggest detrusor underactivity or outlet obstruction.
Transferable rule When a quantitative measure of organ function is given, check whether each candidate diagnosis is compatible with that number before weighing symptoms. Exclude a diagnosis the physiology forbids without arguing from symptoms.
